public_rationale: Contemporary independent testing found substantial commonsense-dependent reasoning failures across several leading models, including o1-preview. Earlier PIQA results document that physical commonsense had also challenged preceding systems. Strong performance on some questions and large gains from tailored prompts qualify the claim, but do not remove the demonstrated reliability problem. This supports the ordinary reading of 'still dodgy'; it does not establish that models lack all commonsense or that progress had stopped.
limitations: Commonsense is broader than the tasks tested.
The decisive contemporary study was a preprint.
The historical and contemporary benchmarks are not directly comparable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Commonsense reasoning in current AI systems remains unreliable, as it long has been.

statement.excerpt: Commonsense reasoning is still dodgy, as it has long been, as Ernie Davis and I just reviewed here..
statement.document_title: Why I don’t share Sam Altman’s confidence that AGI is basically a solved problem

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that contemporary general-purpose language models still make substantial, repeatable mistakes when reasoning about everyday situations. It does not mean they fail every commonsense task or have made no progress.
The surrounding discussion identifies frontier language models as the principal subject.

Because no reporting period is specified and benchmark evaluations are episodic, use the latest completed calendar year and the days through publication: 2024-01-01 through 2025-01-06. Earlier evaluations provide historical context for 'as it has long been'.
No numerical reliability threshold is supplied. Assess whether systematic failures remain across multiple leading models on credible commonsense evaluations.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations demonstrate substantial, repeatable commonsense failures across leading language models, with earlier research documenting comparable limitations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad contemporary evaluations establish consistently reliable commonsense reasoning across varied everyday situations, and the alleged failures are shown to be invalid, obsolete, or confined to unrepresentative systems.

evidence.excerpt: even the latest models lack the ability to effectively apply ToM reasoning
evidence.locator: Section 5.1, Judgment of behavior; Table 2; Section 5.3
evidence.explanation: SimpleToM tests everyday situations requiring inferences about what people can perceive and know. GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Llama-3.1-405B scored only 10–24.9% on behavior judgments; o1-preview reached 59.5%. However, leading models exceeded 95% on mental-state questions, and tailored reminders plus reasoning prompts substantially improved applied reasoning.

PIQA documents an earlier gap in reasoning about ordinary physical interactions. It supports the historical background, but its older models and different benchmark cannot establish January 2025 performance or an unchanged error rate.

evidence.excerpt: the o1 model has achieved the best performance on most datasets.
evidence.locator: Abstract; experimental task definitions in version 2, Section 3.1
evidence.explanation: The study documents improvements with o1, limiting any interpretation that reasoning had made no progress. Its commonsense category uses HotpotQA and constrained text generation, so it does not directly overturn SimpleToM's everyday social-reasoning failures.
